note: Fri 4 Sep 2026, ~07:50 SGT pre-Asia-open run (before SGX 09:00/HKEX 09:30, covering Thu 3 Sep's US close). Thursday was a second straight strong rally (S&P +1.06%, VIX -5.79% to 14.32) driven specifically by Fed Governor Waller's dovish pre-market remarks. No SMIC/Tencent/Singapore-bank-specific headlines dated within the strict last 24-48h were found -- the freshest single-name Asia catalysts are Wednesday's earnings-season backdrop and Thursday's index-level moves; flagged rather than padded with stale items.

items.headline: Fed's Waller signals he could back a September rate hold, driving Thursday's rally
items.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in pre-market remarks (8:30am ET) he could support holding rates steady this month 'so long as upcoming inflation data doesn't produce surprises.' Implied September-hike odds fell from roughly 63% to 50%, and the 10y yield eased to ~4.77%. Rate-sensitive names led the rally (Oracle +5.7%, Palantir +7.7%, financials broadly higher).
items.actionable: Reduced Sept-hike odds directly drove Thursday's broad rally and the silver/gold miner extension (SLV +2.51%, GDX +3.95%) -- Friday's NFP (cons 55K vs -23K prior) is now the decisive print for whether this dovish repricing holds into the Sep 15-16 FOMC.

items.headline: Barrick weighs delaying North America gold IPO to 2027 amid shareholder revolt -- explains its lone miner-complex decline
items.summary: Bloomberg reported Barrick Mining is considering pushing its planned North American gold-asset spin-off/IPO from 2026 to 2027. Several large shareholders (VanEck, Mackenzie Financial, Franklin among them) have publicly opposed Chairman John Thornton's separation strategy, with some calling for his resignation. Barrick fell 5.34% Thursday even as every other tracked gold miner rallied.
items.actionable: Confirms the GDX/miners basket's Barrick component is an idiosyncratic governance story, not a read-through to NEM/AG/PAAS/HL/SILJ, which all continued rallying the same session -- no change to the broader miners thesis.

items.headline: US strikes Iranian tankers and ~100 IRGC-linked sites; Iran retaliates with missiles/drones on Gulf bases -- Hormuz transits collapse
items.summary: The US struck two Iranian government tankers plus roughly 100 IRGC-linked air-defense, radar, drone-launch and mine-laying sites on 2 Sep. Iran retaliated with roughly 25 ballistic missiles (about half reaching Jordanian airspace, mostly intercepted) and drones targeting US-linked bases in Bahrain, Kuwait and Erbil. Strait of Hormuz transits have collapsed to single digits per 24 hours from a pre-crisis pace near 138/day.
items.actionable: A live, still-escalating conflict despite Thursday's market calm -- keeps a residual safe-haven bid under gold/silver and a supply-risk premium under oil, while remaining a headline-risk overhang for HK tech and broader risk assets.

items.headline: Silver holds above $66/oz, +60.8% y/y, as Trump downplays follow-through on Iran strikes
items.summary: Silver traded at $66.21/oz Thursday morning (+1.1% on the day) after President Trump said a 'very heavy attack' on Iran would not persist, easing immediate escalation fears while a geopolitical risk premium remains in the metal. Silver is up roughly 60.8% year-over-year and 14.7% over the trailing month.
items.actionable: Directly supports the levered silver/miners book -- the Hormuz conflict is acting as a live tailwind on top of the existing dovish-Fed-driven bull move, though Trump's 'brief' framing caps near-term upside pending Friday's NFP.

items.headline: Oil heads for biggest weekly gain since July on Hormuz disruption fears; WTI near $92, Brent near $95
items.summary: WTI rose toward $92/bbl (roughly +9% on the week) and Brent traded near $95 as renewed US-Iran hostilities raised fears of prolonged Hormuz disruption; the rally cooled slightly Thursday after Trump signaled the strikes would be brief. Diesel prices hit their highest level since 2022.
items.actionable: Rising energy costs plus Hormuz risk premium reinforce the case for the portfolio's large cash pile and hard-asset (gold/silver) tilt as an inflation and geopolitical hedge -- a factor the Fed will weigh alongside Friday's NFP.

items.headline: Bitcoin reclaims $81,000 on ~$415M short squeeze and renewed ETF inflows
items.summary: BTC rallied nearly 5% intraday to reclaim $81K, driven by large short liquidations (~$415M) and renewed institutional buying; spot Bitcoin ETFs logged over $100M in net inflows on 2 Sep, reversing prior-session redemptions. Elevated 10y yields (~4.77%) and oil prices remain crosscurrents.
items.actionable: Confirms Thursday's rally was a broad risk-on move (equities, gold, silver, BTC together), not solely a precious-metals story -- but the Sep 15 CLARITY Act cloture vote's deteriorating odds (~19.5%, down from a 58% high) remain the dominant near-term crypto-specific risk to size against.

items.headline: Hang Seng rises 0.6% to 25,459, Tencent +0.4%, partially reversing Wednesday's US-rally lag
items.summary: The Hang Seng gained 0.6% to 25,459 Thursday, rebounding on the softer US data and dovish Fed signaling. Tencent (+0.4%), Lenovo (+1.1%), MiniMax (+1.0%) and AIA (+1.8%) led gainers, partially reversing Wednesday's -1.19% Tencent decline even as the US rallied hard that session.
items.actionable: Suggests Wednesday's HK-vs-US divergence was a one-day lag rather than a new bearish trend for the HK tech book, though HK remains more macro-data-sensitive right now than a pure momentum play.

items.headline: Xiaomi's September product blitz (Xiaomi 18, SkyNomad EV, YU7 GT) arrives under a margin question
items.summary: Xiaomi is set to launch the Xiaomi 18 phone series and SkyNomad EV series in September, alongside the high-performance YU7 GT (~990hp). August EV deliveries topped 30,000 with a 2026 target of 550,000 units, but shares remain roughly 54% below their 52-week high on investor concern about margin sustainability as EV/IoT businesses scale.
items.actionable: Explains Xiaomi's -2.21% underperformance versus Tencent/SMIC in Wednesday's HK session -- the market is discounting EV-margin execution risk even as unit deliveries scale; the September launch cadence is the key near-term catalyst to watch.

items.headline: China formalizes public reporting mechanism for rare-earth export-control violations as the Nov 10 suspension deadline approaches
items.summary: China's broadest rare-earth export controls (announced Oct 2025) remain suspended until 10 Nov 2026 under the current trade truce, but the earlier April-2025 licensing regime for seven rare-earth elements remains fully in force. MOFCOM Announcement No. 26 (2026) formalized a public whistleblower/reporting mechanism for violations, signaling more active enforcement rather than de-escalation.
items.actionable: The Nov 10, 2026 suspension expiry is now just over two months away and remains the single most important date for the rare-earth watchlist -- increased Chinese enforcement activity supports the ex-China de-risking thesis (MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels) as structural rather than purely cyclical.

items.headline: MP Materials, Lynas and Energy Fuels post concrete operational milestones beyond the policy headlines
items.summary: MP Materials' Materials segment revenue jumped 80% half-on-half on surging NdPr production; its DoD-backed 10X Magnetics facility in Texas (commissioning 2028) will supply GM. Lynas produced 3,407 MT of NdPr in 1H FY26, targeting 12,000 tpa at full ramp. Energy Fuels expects commercial-scale dysprosium/terbium output at its White Mesa Mill in Q4 2026 -- a first for US heavy rare-earth separation.
items.actionable: These operational milestones (not just policy headlines) de-risk the rare-earth watchlist -- Energy Fuels' Q4 heavy-REE production start is the nearest-term concrete catalyst to track.

items.headline: Singapore REITs post strong H1 results as falling financing costs flow through to distributions
items.summary: Suntec REIT's DPU jumped 23.9% to S$0.01936 on lower financing costs and rental reversions of 14.3% (retail)/9.5% (office). Frasers Centrepoint Trust's gross revenue rose 20.3% to S$221.9M. AIMS APAC REIT posted a 1.1% DPU rise with 93.3% portfolio occupancy.
items.actionable: Falling financing costs are visibly flowing through to distributions across the SG REIT sleeve -- the fundamental case for owning SREITs into a rate-cutting-leaning Fed cycle, reinforced by this reporting season.

items.headline: DBS and OCBC post record 1H26 income on wealth-management fee strength
items.summary: OCBC delivered record quarterly total income of S$3.8B (+5% y/y) in 1Q26, while DBS posted record total income of S$5.95B with non-interest income up 10% to S$2.45B on record wealth-management fees of S$907M. Both banks outperformed the STI in 1H26.
items.actionable: Confirms the structural earnings backdrop for the SGX bank holdings remains strong (record wealth fees, resilient NIMs) heading into today's Asia open, though no bank-specific headline was found within the last 24-48h this run.
